scenarios.adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10045: insured's warehouse (Flood Zone 2) suffered flood damage on 15 June 2024 when water entered from a nearby river during heavy rainfall. No prior flood event at this location this policy year. Claimed amount GBP 180,000.
scenarios.why: One good search on the flood sub-limit/deductible clauses (Endorsement 1) should settle this in a single retrieve -- the case the fixed workflow is built for.

scenarios.adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10046: insured's distribution centre flooded again on 20 July 2024, six weeks (42 days) after an earlier flood at the same site on 8 June 2024. No record of the flood barriers, non-return valves or sump pumps having been tested in the 60 days before the second event.
scenarios.why: A generic 'flood damage' search surfaces Endorsement 1's sub-limit/deductible clauses, not the sequential-event exclusion in Endorsement 4 (clause 4.3, Exclusion Code E-17) or its clause 4.4 carve-out -- correctly deciding this claim needs a second, more targeted search.

scenarios.adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10047: a ransomware attack on 3 September 2024 triggered a fire in the server room that caused physical damage to computer hardware and the surrounding building fabric. No ransom was paid and no data was lost; the insured seeks cover for the physical fire damage only.
scenarios.why: The broad cyber exclusion (Endorsement 2, Section 2) reads like a clean denial until Section 3's write-back is found: physical fire/explosion damage resulting from a Cyber Incident is carved back in. Tests whether the pipeline finds and correctly weighs the write-back, not just the exclusion.

scenarios.adjuster_notes: Claim ref ABC/2024/778: business interruption following a burst water main that caused a production outage lasting 5 days from 2 November 2024. The outage was notified to the risk manager on 25 November 2024.
scenarios.why: The claim reference is not in CLM-YYYY-NNNNN form, so check_assertions' claim_number_format check should fail and stay failed -- neither pipeline can invent a number the notes never state. Separately, the outage (5 days) exceeds the 72-hour waiting period and was notified within the 30-day window, so coverage itself should still resolve.

scenarios.adjuster_notes: Claim CLM-2024-10048: insured is claiming for a company vehicle stolen from the staff car park on 10 August 2024. Claimed amount GBP 32,000.
scenarios.why: Motor theft is outside this endorsement pack entirely (property/liability/cyber/business-interruption only). summarize_claim has no relevance gate (unlike /ask), so this checks whether either pipeline actually recognises out-of-scope circumstances or confidently cites an unrelated clause -- a known gap worth reporting honestly either way.

GLOBAL MANUFACTURING LTD

COMMERCIAL PROPERTY AND LIABILITY ENDORSEMENT PACK
Policy Number GML-2024-88213. Period of Insurance: 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025, both dates inclusive at the address of the Insured. This pack records every endorsement attached to the policy and supersedes any endorsement schedule issued previously.

ENDORSEMENT NO. 1 - FLOOD SUB-LIMIT AMENDMENT
Effective from 1 June 2024. In consideration of the additional premium of GBP 42,750 the following amendments are made to the Property Damage section of the policy.

1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 Flood means the escape of water from the normal confines of any natural or artificial watercourse, lake, reservoir, canal or dam, or inundation from the sea, whether driven by storm or otherwise.

1.2 Flood Zone means any location identified as Zone 2 or Zone 3 on the Environment Agency Flood Map for Planning current at the inception of this endorsement.

2. AMENDMENT TO LIMIT
The sub-limit applicable to loss or damage caused by Flood is amended from GBP 2,500,000 to GBP 5,000,000 in the annual aggregate. The revised sub-limit applies to all insured locations combined and is part of, and not in addition to, the policy limit of GBP 40,000,000 any one occurrence.

3. DEDUCTIBLE
A deductible of GBP 250,000 each and every loss applies to loss or damage caused by Flood at any location within a Flood Zone. At all other locations the standard property deductible of GBP 50,000 each and every loss continues to apply.

SECTION 4 - CONDITIONS APPLYING TO THIS ENDORSEMENT

3. DEDUCTIBLE
A deductible of GBP 250,000 each and every loss applies to loss or damage caused by Flood at any location within a Flood Zone. At all other locations the standard property deductible of GBP 50,000 each and every loss continues to apply.

SECTION 4 - CONDITIONS APPLYING TO THIS ENDORSEMENT

4.1 Flood Defence Maintenance
The Insured shall maintain all demountable flood barriers, non-return valves and sump pumps at each insured location in good and effective working order, and shall test them at intervals of not more than six months. A written record of each test shall be kept for a period of three years and produced to the Insurer on request.

4.2 Exclusions
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the policy, this endorsement does not cover loss, damage, cost or expense arising directly or indirectly out of:

(a) subsidence, ground heave or landslip, whether or not caused or contributed to by Flood; (b) loss of or damage to growing crops, standing timber, or livestock in the open; (c) any property in the course of construction, erection or installation where the contract value exceeds GBP 1,000,000; (d) loss or damage to stock stored below ground level unless raised at least 150 millimetres above the finished floor level; (e) any fine, penalty or punitive damages levied by a regulator following a Flood event.

4.2.1 Erosion of the sub-limit
Each payment made under this endorsement, including any payment for professional fees and debris removal, erodes the annual aggregate sub-limit stated in clause 2. Once the annual aggregate sub-limit is exhausted no further payment shall be made under this endorsement for the remainder of the Period of Insurance.

(a) any Cyber Act or Cyber Incident, including but not limited to any action taken in controlling, preventing, suppressing or remediating any Cyber Act or Cyber Incident, and including the cost of any forensic investigation commissioned by the Insured or by any regulator, and including any sum paid or payable to a third party by way of settlement, judgment, award or contractual indemnity in respect of such an act or incident, whether or not the Insured admitted liability;

3. Subject to all other terms of the policy, this exclusion shall not apply to physical loss of or physical damage to insured property arising from fire or explosion which itself results from a Cyber Incident, provided that the fire or explosion is not the result of a Cyber Act committed with intent to cause physical damage.

ENDORSEMENT NO. 3 - BUSINESS INTERRUPTION AMENDMENTS
Effective from 1 October 2024. The Business Interruption section is amended as set out below. All other terms, conditions and exclusions remain unaltered.

1. WAITING PERIOD
A waiting period of 72 consecutive hours applies to each and every claim under the Business Interruption section. No indemnity is payable in respect of any interruption that is remedied within the waiting period.

2. INDEMNITY PERIOD
